title: Train a flow on straight lines, then straighten it
brief: Build the optimal-transport path and its loss, three ODE solvers with their convergence orders, the bridge to the diffusion convention, minibatch OT pairing, and a straightness measure that shows what one round of reflow does.
hints: In ot_path, a per-example time of shape (B,) must become (B, 1, ..., 1) before it multiplies a (B, C, T) batch: t.reshape(tuple(t.shape) + (1,) * (x0.ndim - t.ndim)). Leave a float alone.
The Gaussian marginal field is mu + (t s^2 - (1 - t)) / ((1 - t)^2 + t^2 s^2) * (x - t mu). One Euler step from t = 0 therefore lands exactly on mu.
Compute each step's start time as k / n_steps rather than adding dt repeatedly, so the last step ends on t = 1 exactly.
Midpoint evaluates the field at x + (h/2) k1 and time t + h/2. RK4 combines four slopes with weights 1, 2, 2, 1, divided by 6.
In to_diffusion, recover data = x_t + (1 - t) u and noise = x_t - t u first. Matching the signal-to-noise ratio t^2 / (1 - t)^2 gives alpha_bar = t^2 / (t^2 + (1 - t)^2).
scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the (n, n) matrix of squared distances returns (rows, cols); cols is the permutation.
